subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add shared config for routing internal lifecycle/tool-error/system warning notifications to an operator target, or keep the supported behavior as suppression/logging only?
rationale: The source issue is real, but adding `messages` routing config changes shared delivery semantics and needs maintainer intent under the repository's high bar for new config surfaces.

options.title: Approve minimal opt-in routing
options.body: Add a default-preserving internal warning target with a small category set and focused upgrade-safe docs/tests.

options.title: Keep suppression-only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` plus logs as the intended UX and close or narrow routing requests.

options.title: Defer category design
options.body: Leave this open until maintainers define warning categories, target syntax, and per-channel behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve minimal opt-in routing
recommendation.body: Add a default-preserving internal warning target with a small category set and focused upgrade-safe docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent merged work on the exact `messages.suppressToolErrors` dispatch path makes this the closest routing candidate from current history.
